title: Voice providers declare their traits; failover and routes stop naming them
acceptance: Trait table is total and truthful: for every id in VOICE_PROVIDER_ORDER, VOICE_PROVIDER_TRAITS[id] exists; openai = { transport: 'webrtc', prompt: 'server', asrKeywords: false, relay: true, selfHostable: false, modelIdentity: 'realtime-model' } and elevenlabs = { transport: 'websocket', prompt: 'client-override', asrKeywords: true, relay: false, selfHostable: true, modelIdentity: 'agent-id' }. The module imports nothing server-side, so preflight.ts (browser code) can read it.
failoverOrder('openai', { openai: true, elevenlabs: true }, () => false) returns ['elevenlabs']; with elevenlabs unavailable it returns []; the preferred provider never appears in its own list.

The free-to-paid rule moves into the helper. connectWithFailover({ preferred: 'elevenlabs', isFree: (id) => id === 'elevenlabs', availability: both true }): the elevenlabs stub throws E, so the call rejects with E, and the openai stub is never dialed (calls === ['elevenlabs']). Today the helper fails over here, and only the route's `{ ...voiceAvailability(), openai: false }` override at connect/route.ts:445 stops it.

More than two providers, through an injected order and trait table with a fake third id 'local'. If the preferred 'openai' throws, the first alternate throws and the second resolves, then the second serves: failedOver true, calls in VOICE_PROVIDER_ORDER order. If every provider throws, the PREFERRED provider's original error is rethrown, which is today's contract. Today otherProvider (connect-failover.ts:39-41) can only name one alternate and maps every non-openai id to 'openai'.

Derived vocabulary: coerceProviderId('elevenlabs') === 'elevenlabs', coerceProviderId('ELEVENLABS') === null, coerceProviderId('x', 'openai') === 'openai'. Object.keys(voiceAvailability()) equals VOICE_PROVIDER_ORDER as a set, with the env both set and unset.

Behaviour is unchanged where it matters. voicePreflightCode({ isSecureContext: true, hasMediaDevices: true, hasGetUserMedia: true, hasRTCPeerConnection: false }, 'elevenlabs') === null, and for 'openai' it returns 'VOICE_PREFLIGHT_NO_WEBRTC'. isSelfHostedProvider('elevenlabs', { ELEVENLABS_BASE_URL: 'http://127.0.0.1:8080' }) === true and isSelfHostedProvider('openai', same env) === false. voiceSessionModel('elevenlabs') returns ELEVENLABS_AGENT_ID.

Relay is a trait, not a hardcoded name. relayProvider({ openai: true, elevenlabs: true }) === 'openai' and relayProvider({ openai: false, elevenlabs: true }) === null. The intake voice-connect 503 still answers INTAKE_VOICE_NOT_CONFIGURED with { provider: 'openai', need: ['OPENAI_API_KEY'] }, the need of the first relay-capable provider, so the wire is byte-identical. The rate-limit contract's pinned `adapter.connect(` and `const voiceConnectLimit = 6;` still match.

Names leave the seams: a source-level check over app/api/interview/connect/route.ts, app/api/intake/[id]/voice-connect/route.ts, app/_lib/voice/{connect-failover,self-hosted,minute-prices,preflight,types}.ts finds 0 matches of /[!=]== "(openai|elevenlabs)"/, 'openai: false' or 'getVoiceAdapter("openai")'. Today it finds 9: connect-failover.ts:40, minute-prices.ts:80, preflight.ts:70, self-hosted.ts:92, types.ts:19, connect/route.ts:406, :445, :509, intake voice-connect/route.ts:73.
premise: app/_lib/voice/types.ts:8 VoiceProviderId is a closed two-member union; types.ts:18-20 coerceProviderId re-lists both names by hand instead of reading VOICE_PROVIDER_ORDER (types.ts:29).
app/_lib/voice/index.ts:22-24 voiceAvailability() hand-lists `{ openai: ..., elevenlabs: ... }`, which is a third copy of the provider list.

app/_lib/voice/connect-failover.ts:39-41 otherProvider returns `id === "openai" ? "elevenlabs" : "openai"`. The failover at :79-88 tries exactly ONE alternate, so a third provider would be unreachable as a rescue and every non-openai id maps to openai.

app/api/interview/connect/route.ts:440-445: the rule that a free self-hosted session must never be rescued onto a paid provider is enforced in the route as `isSelfHostedProvider(provider) ? { ...voiceAvailability(), openai: false } : voiceAvailability()`. It hardcodes that 'openai' is the paid one, and connectWithFailover itself does not know the rule.

app/api/interview/connect/route.ts:405-406 resolveAgentPrompt returns null when `served !== "elevenlabs"`, and :508-509 computes asrKeywords only when `served === "elevenlabs"`. Both are provider TRAITS (where the prompt is delivered; whether client-side ASR bias exists) encoded as names.

app/api/intake/[id]/voice-connect/route.ts:73 `getVoiceAdapter("openai")`: relay is honored only by OpenAI (types.ts:103-105 comment, openai.ts:210-211). The knowledge that relay is openai-only lives in comments at :59-66 and in the rate-limit contract's prose (app/api/rate-limit-contract.test.ts:915-921).

app/_lib/voice/self-hosted.ts:88-93 isSelfHostedProvider is `provider === "elevenlabs" && isSelfHostedVoice(env)`. It is a money decision with 4 external callers that keep their signature: complete/route.ts:382, connect/route.ts:208, simulate/route.ts:91, jobs/[id]/interview-kit/rehearse/route.ts:135.
app/_lib/voice/preflight.ts:70 `provider === "openai" && !env.hasRTCPeerConnection`: the transport trait is encoded as a name, in browser-safe code.
app/_lib/voice/minute-prices.ts:79-82 voiceSessionModel branches `provider === "openai"` to pick the model identity.

Disjoint from r08: challenge-r08 voice-interview-components/A ('One call-transport contract') writes only app/_components/voice/** (the CLIENT half: 7 provider-name branches in VoiceInterview.tsx). This card is the SERVER half and touches no file in any r08 write set. preflight.ts keeps its exported signature, which VoiceInterview.tsx calls.
rollback: A single commit series of one new pure module plus mechanical call-site substitutions, with no schema, no stored value, no wire field and no catalog key. `git revert` restores the name branches byte-for-byte. The connect-failover contract tests that exist today (connect-failover.test.ts) must pass unchanged before and after, which is what makes the revert safe.
runner_up: One voice-meter module for the three planes: minute-prices.ts:47-58, tts-prices.ts:33-44 and stt-prices.ts:46-57 each re-implement the same 'operator override env, refuse malformed, warn, fall back to estimate' parser and the same known-zero-vs-unknown rule. It would be one priced-unit table keyed by plane (minute / kchar / hour).
body:
## Summary
The server side of the voice plane names its providers in 9 places outside the adapters, and three of those names carry policy. The failover rescue can only reach 'the other one'. The rule that a free session is never rescued onto a paid provider lives in one route as `openai: false`. Where the interviewer prompt is delivered, and whether ASR keyword bias applies, are branches on `"elevenlabs"`. This card puts a browser-safe trait table beside VOICE_PROVIDER_ORDER, moves the free-to-paid rule into connectWithFailover, and lets failover walk an ordered list of alternates. Every route then asks what a provider can do, never which one it is.

## Description
The registry technique engine-abstraction (voice-io) says: "The tell that the abstraction has failed is an engine's name appearing in surface code." Here the adapters (openai.ts, elevenlabs.ts) are clean, but the knowledge of what each one IS has leaked into the seams around them:
- connect-failover.ts:39-41 `otherProvider` hardcodes a two-member complement, and the rescue at :79-88 tries exactly one alternate.
- connect/route.ts:445 enforces the money rule (a self-hosted session skipped /simulate's meter gate, so it must never land on a paid provider) by zeroing `openai` in an availability map. The helper that performs the failover does not know the rule, so any second caller of connectWithFailover would silently lose it.
- connect/route.ts:406 and :509 decide the prompt plane and the ASR bias by name.
- intake voice-connect/route.ts:73 hardcodes the only relay-capable provider.
- self-hosted.ts:92, preflight.ts:70, minute-prices.ts:80 and types.ts:19 each re-encode one trait or the list itself.

What this costs, counted: a third realtime provider (Azure-brokered Realtime, or a native self-hosted id beside the Gravitone-compatible ElevenLabs path in self-hosted.ts) means editing these 9 sites across 7 files. Two of those edits are money rules (the failover exclusion and isSelfHostedProvider) that no compiler error points at, because `otherProvider` and the `openai: false` literal both still typecheck with a wider union.

The move is a new app/_lib/voice/provider-traits.ts: pure data keyed by VoiceProviderId, `{ transport, prompt, asrKeywords, relay, selfHostable, modelIdentity }`, plus `failoverOrder(preferred, availability, isFree)` and `relayProvider(availability)`. coerceProviderId and voiceAvailability are derived from VOICE_PROVIDER_ORDER. connectWithFailover gains an `isFree` seam, defaulting to isSelfHostedProvider, and walks failoverOrder. The route's `openai: false` is deleted because the helper now holds the rule. isSelfHostedProvider keeps its signature for its 4 callers. The adapter interface, the /connect response shape, the rate-limit pins (`connectWithFailover(`, `adapter.connect(`, `const connectLimit = isSelfHostedProvider(provider) ? 120 : 6;`) and the r08 client files are untouched.

Out of scope: the client shell (r08 voice-interview-components/A owns that half), the adapters' own fetch code, and the TTS/STT packages, which already have registries.

## Flow
1. Write provider-traits.test.ts and extend connect-failover.test.ts with the 8 acceptance cases (the free-to-paid case and the three-provider case are red today).
2. Add provider-traits.ts with no server imports (preflight.ts is browser code).
3. Derive coerceProviderId (types.ts) and voiceAvailability (index.ts) from VOICE_PROVIDER_ORDER.
4. connect-failover.ts: add the `isFree` option; iterate failoverOrder; keep 'rethrow the preferred error' and the resolveAgentPrompt-outside-the-trigger ordering (:90-101). Keep `otherProvider` as a deprecated alias for one release, or delete it with its one test at connect-failover.test.ts:40-43.
5. connect/route.ts: :406 becomes `traits(served).prompt === 'server'`, :445 becomes plain voiceAvailability(), and :509 becomes `traits(served).asrKeywords`.
6. intake voice-connect: resolve through relayProvider, then call `adapter.connect(` (the pinned text), and keep the same 503 body.
7. self-hosted.ts:92, preflight.ts:70 and minute-prices.ts:80 read the trait.
8. Docs: add a 'provider traits' paragraph to docs/features/interviews/README.md and a line in docs/features/intake/README.md saying the relay provider is derived.

## Expected impact
Adding a realtime provider becomes one adapter plus one trait row. The failover and self-hosting money rules are held in the one helper that acts on them, and a unit test proves it, instead of an availability-map literal in one route. Paired with r08's client-side transport contract, no voice surface on either side of the wire branches on a vendor name. No behaviour changes for today's two providers, as the unchanged connect-failover suite and the preflight and self-hosted cases show.

## Evaluation
Claim: provider identity no longer decides behaviour outside the adapters; traits do, and the free-to-paid failover rule is enforced by the helper that fails over.
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass (provider-traits.ts does not exist; the source check finds 9 name branches; the free-to-paid case fails over today at the helper level).
After: 8 of 8.
Method: node:test under npm run test:unit (provider-traits.test.ts, connect-failover.test.ts, plus the existing preflight/self-hosted/minute-prices/openai-session suites unchanged), then tsc, lint, lint:ts-ratchet and the rate-limit contract test. No perf exposure: nothing is added to app/page.tsx or the task-hub graph, and provider-traits.ts is a leaf module.
Result: pending build.
Gate: architecture.

title: Voice joins the system strip: a free mint proves each provider, priced
acceptance: No probe, no green. With OPENAI_API_KEY unset, ELEVENLABS_API_KEY and ELEVENLABS_AGENT_ID set, and no probe run, buildVoiceReadiness(...) returns openai { state: 'absent', need: ['OPENAI_API_KEY'] } and elevenlabs { state: 'unchecked' }. No row is 'ready' until a mint has succeeded. Today the only signal, voiceAvailability(), would report elevenlabs: true.

The price in force is shown, with where it came from. ELEVENLABS_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8080 gives elevenlabs billing { kind: 'self-hosted', usdPerMin: 0 }. KP_VOICE_MINUTE_USD_OPENAI='0.2' gives openai { kind: 'per-minute', usdPerMin: 0.2, source: 'override' }. Unset gives { usdPerMin: 0.15, source: 'estimate' }. The '$0.12' value that voiceMinutePriceUsd refuses gives source 'estimate', plus a 'malformedOverride' flag naming KP_VOICE_MINUTE_USD_OPENAI.

Mint failures are born typed, and the log text is unchanged. With a stubbed fetch, OpenAiVoiceAdapter.connect on a 401 rejects with VoiceMintError { provider: 'openai', cause: 'auth', status: 401 } whose message still starts 'OpenAI client_secrets 401:'. An ElevenLabs 404 gives cause 'not_found'. An AbortSignal TimeoutError gives 'timeout'. A fetch TypeError (connection refused on a dead self-hosted service) gives 'unreachable'. A 200 with no signed_url, or a secret with an unusable expires_at, gives 'malformed'. connectWithFailover still fails over on any of them, and its existing tests pass unchanged.

A live probe with injected adapters and clock: openai resolves after 40 ms and elevenlabs rejects VoiceMintError('not_found'). The result is openai { state: 'ready', latencyMs: 40 } and elevenlabs { state: 'broken', cause: 'not_found', remedy: { kind: 'env', vars: ['ELEVENLABS_AGENT_ID', 'ELEVENLABS_BASE_URL'] } }. The two probes run under Promise.allSettled, so one hung provider (resolved only by its adapter's 15 s timeout) does not hide the other's verdict.

A silent reroute is made visible. With KP_VOICE_PROVIDER=elevenlabs, the ElevenLabs keys unset and OPENAI_API_KEY set, report.preference is { requested: 'elevenlabs', honored: false, defaultProvider: 'openai' }. This is the case where index.ts:44-46 silently drops the preference and every new link from interview-invite.ts:98-99 goes to OpenAI.

Probe memory without polling mints. A GET within VOICE_PROBE_TTL_MS of a POST returns the POST's states with checkedAt. After the TTL (injected clock), the same rows read 'unchecked' again. A GET never calls adapter.connect (the counting double stays at 0), so opening the Billing tab spends no provider round trips.

Route door and projection. POST /api/voice/readiness with no home-org session returns 401 (requireHomeOrgReader). The 7th POST from one IP inside 10 min returns 429 TOO_MANY_REQUESTS. A 200 body never contains the minted credential: JSON.stringify(body) does not contain the stub's clientSecret, signedUrl or callsUrl strings. An unexpected throw answers VOICE_READINESS_FAILED through safeJsonError.

Failover history, tenant-scoped. Fixture: sessions A1 and A2 in workspace A with failover_from 'elevenlabs' and provider 'openai', started 2 days ago; A3 in workspace A, started 9 days ago; B1 in workspace B. countInterviewFailovers('A', sevenDaysAgo) returns [{ from: 'elevenlabs', to: 'openai', count: 2 }], and B1 never appears in A's answer.
premise: app/_lib/voice/types.ts:126-128 missingVoiceEnv checks only that env NAMES are set, and index.ts:22-24 voiceAvailability() is built from it. A revoked or mistyped OPENAI_API_KEY, or a wrong ELEVENLABS_AGENT_ID, therefore reads 'available' until a candidate opens a link, and the failure first surfaces as INTERVIEW_CONNECT_FAILED on the candidate's /connect (app/api/interview/connect/route.ts:547).

The other two voice planes already speak three states, 'absent (offer setup) is not broken': packages/voice-tts/src/types.ts:35-41 and packages/voice-stt/src/types.ts:65-71, served by GET /api/tts at app/api/tts/route.ts:57-63. The realtime plane, which the code itself calls 'the most expensive operation in the system' (connect/route.ts:185-187), is the only one reduced to a boolean.

The operator's system strip names the text engines and no voice engine. app/features/settings/billing/spend/SpendEngineFacts.tsx:164-171 renders Gemini and Claude CLI from ops.engines, which /api/ops fills from engineAvailability() (app/api/ops/route.ts:102; app/_lib/engine-preflight.ts:17-22 has only gemini and claudeCli). engine-preflight.ts:8-10 names voiceAvailability as 'the same idea' and never surfaces it.

app/_lib/voice/index.ts:44-46 onboardedVoiceProvider drops a KP_VOICE_PROVIDER preference whose provider is unconfigured, with no signal. pickDefaultProvider (index.ts:32-37) then routes every new invite (app/_lib/interview-invite.ts:98-99) to the next configured provider, and the operator who chose ElevenLabs is never told.

Failovers are stored and shown nowhere. connect/route.ts:456-465 writes failover_from, and app/_lib/db/interviews.ts:168-172 documents it as the recruiter's lost choice, but `grep -rln failoverFrom app/features app/_components` returns nothing.

The price in force is invisible. voiceMinutePriceUsd (app/_lib/voice/minute-prices.ts:47-58) resolves override vs estimate and warns only on the console, and voiceMinuteCostUsd (:66-72) zeroes self-hosted. An operator cannot see which number the ledger is using.

Adapter failures today are untyped Errors carrying the status in the message: app/_lib/voice/openai.ts:315, :320, :326, :335; app/_lib/voice/elevenlabs.ts:37, :50, :53. Without this card, any classifier would be a regex over English, which is the shape the r08 llm-inference-runtime/B card is removing elsewhere.

A probe mint opens no conversation. OpenAI's credential is asked to expire in OPENAI_SECRET_TTL_SEC = 120 (app/_lib/voice/openai.ts:106) and is useless without the SDP POST. ElevenLabs returns a signed URL that is never dialed (elevenlabs.ts:40-54). Both adapters already bound the mint at 15 s (openai.ts:113, elevenlabs.ts:24).

Auth and perf posture. app/_lib/auth/public-routes.ts has no /api/voice entry (only /api/interview/connect at :113), so the new route is gated by default and additionally calls requireHomeOrgReader like /api/ops (app/api/ops/route.ts:3). The strip is not in app/page.tsx's static graph: BillingTab.tsx:39 loads the spend section through dynamic(). It is not in the task-hub graph either.

Surfaces that display voice availability, named per the r07 lesson. GET /api/interview/connect (connect/route.ts:77-79) feeds the candidate picker and start gate (app/_components/voice/availability-gate.ts:35-45, VoiceSettings.tsx). GET /api/intake/[id]/voice-connect (route.ts:36-40) feeds the intake mic. Both deliberately stay env-level: a candidate page must never trigger a provider mint. No refusal is added and no stored status changes, so neither needs an edit, and both are outside every r08 write set.
rollback: Additive. It adds one gated route, one pure module, one error subclass that keeps the old message text, one read-only store query and one strip row. Reverting the series removes the row and the route. The adapters go back to throwing plain Error with identical messages, so the connect route's safeJsonError log lines never change in either direction. No schema, no migration and no stored value are touched. The four catalogs lose their appended key block in the same revert.
runner_up: An interview-lab audition: dial the same scripted opening line through both realtime providers side by side, the way TtsComparePanel does for synthesis. Traded away because the dial lives in VoiceInterview.tsx, which both r08 voice-interview-components cards are rewriting right now.
body:
## Summary
An operator today learns that a voice provider is broken when a candidate does. Readiness is 'is the env var set' (types.ts:126-128), the system strip lists Gemini and the Claude CLI but no voice engine (SpendEngineFacts.tsx:164-171), a stale KP_VOICE_PROVIDER is silently ignored (index.ts:44-46), and the failovers the connect route records (connect/route.ts:456-465) are read by no surface. This card gives the realtime plane the same three honest states the TTS and STT planes already have. It makes 'ready' require evidence, a real credential mint that opens no conversation, triggered by a 'Check now' button. Each provider row also shows the price per minute in force, where that number came from, whether the preferred provider is actually the one new links will use, and how many screens fell back from it this week.

## Description
Registry, health-checks: three-state-outcomes (absent is not broken, and 'could not check' is its own state), probe-design (observe the target, not a proxy: env presence is a proxy) and remediation-affordances (every failure names its fix). From remote-capability-probing: advertised-support-is-not-evidence.

Pieces:
1. **Typed mint failures** (new voice/mint-error.ts). `VoiceMintError extends Error { provider, cause: 'auth'|'not_found'|'timeout'|'unreachable'|'upstream'|'malformed', status? }`, thrown by openai.ts and elevenlabs.ts in place of the plain Errors at the cited lines, with the SAME message strings. connectWithFailover and the connect route's safeJsonError are unaffected because they catch anything.
2. **readiness.ts**, pure and injectable (env, clock, adapters, price fn, failover reader). It holds buildVoiceReadiness(), classifyMintFailure(), the probe-memory cache (VOICE_PROBE_TTL_MS = 10 min, keyed by provider) and the remedy table (auth leads to the key var; not_found to AGENT_ID and BASE_URL; unreachable to BASE_URL, 'is the local service running'; timeout and upstream to 'retry later'). The rows are the states absent / unchecked / ready / broken, plus billing { kind, usdPerMin, source }, preference { requested, honored, defaultProvider } and failovers7d.
3. **GET/POST /api/voice/readiness**, gated by requireHomeOrgReader. GET is cheap: env, prices, preference, the failover count for the caller's workspace, and any cached probe verdicts. POST runs the live probes with Promise.allSettled and a fixed 'readiness probe' instruction, no session token and no tools. It is limited per IP to 6 per 10 min (a new rate-limit-contract row). The response is a projection with no credential fields. New STORE code VOICE_READINESS_FAILED in api-response.ts plus errors.VOICE_READINESS_FAILED in 4 catalogs. The route row comes from `npm run api:docs`.
4. **countInterviewFailovers(workspaceId, sinceIso)** in app/_lib/db/interviews.ts. It is a read-only GROUP BY failover_from, provider over interview_sessions with `workspace_id = ?`, on the existing scoped table, so there is no tenancy-manifest change. It imports the slice, never the app/_lib/db.ts barrel.
5. **SpendVoiceFacts.tsx**, mounted in BillingSpendPanel beside SpendEngineFacts. It shows one Fact line per provider: dot, product name (a constant, Do-Not-Translate, as at SpendEngineFacts.tsx:31-36), translated state word, the price or 'free, self-hosted', the env vars to set on absent or broken, and 'N screens fell back from X in 7 days'. Above the lines sit a preference line when honored is false and a 'Check now' button with checkedAt. Copy goes under models.system.voice.* in 4 catalogs, and tokens and recipes only (BTN_GHOST, NOTICE).

No read-then-write: the route writes nothing but the in-memory probe memory (last writer wins, harmless) and the limiter. The strip does not change `ok` or the readiness findings that /api/health gates on (readiness.ts is not touched), so a keyless install's boot contract (GET /api/health = 200) is unaffected.

## Flow
1. Tests first: readiness.test.ts (cases 1, 2, 4, 5, 6), additions to openai-session.test.ts and a new ElevenLabs stub case in readiness.test.ts (case 3), route.test.ts (case 7), and a store case in readiness.test.ts using the in-memory DB helper the interviews tests already use (case 8). All red.
2. mint-error.ts, then swap the throws in openai.ts and elevenlabs.ts, keeping the messages.
3. readiness.ts, then the countInterviewFailovers slice query.
4. The route, the rate-limit contract row, the api-response code, `npm run api:docs`.
5. SpendVoiceFacts.tsx and the 4-catalog key block (appended under the shared-surface lock).
6. Docs: the 'Operator readiness' section in docs/features/interviews/README.md and one line in docs/features/billing/README.md for the Spend strip.

## Expected impact
A broken key, a wrong agent id or a dead self-hosted voice service is found by the operator in one click on the Billing tab, instead of by a candidate on a live link. The operator who set KP_VOICE_PROVIDER learns when it is being ignored. The 'fell back from ElevenLabs' fact the connect route has been recording finally reaches a person. The price per minute the ledger bills with is visible, and so is whether it is an estimate. As a side effect, mint failures carry a typed cause that future failover policy (for example 'do not fail over on auth, the other provider will not fix a bad key') can use without a regex.

## Evaluation
Claim: every configured realtime provider has an evidence-based state (absent / unchecked / ready / broken with a cause and a fix), a visible price in force and a visible failover history on the operator's Spend strip, with no mint on page load and no credential in any response.
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass (readiness.ts, mint-error.ts, the route and countInterviewFailovers do not exist).
After: 8 of 8.
Method: node:test under npm run test:unit (readiness.test.ts, route.test.ts, openai-session.test.ts additions, rate-limit-contract.test.ts), then tsc, lint, i18n:check, design:check, api:check and test:perf. Perf exposure: one new route graph (voice slice + api-response + auth), which is expected to sit well under the app/api/**/route.ts group ceiling of 230 modules. Nothing is added to app/page.tsx (BillingTab.tsx:39 dynamic) or to the task-hub graph.
Result: pending build.
Gate: contract.
evidence:
Readiness is env presence only:
  app/_lib/voice/types.ts:126-128  export function missingVoiceEnv(adapter) { return adapter.requiredEnv.filter((name) => !process.env[name]); }
  app/_lib/voice/index.ts:22-24    voiceAvailability() { return { openai: adapters.openai.available(), elevenlabs: adapters.elevenlabs.available() }; }
The TTS plane has three states: packages/voice-tts/src/types.ts:35 '/** Three distinguishable states — absent (offer setup) is not broken', :40-41 `{ state: "absent"; reason; setup? } | { state: "broken"; reason }`.
The strip shows no voice: SpendEngineFacts.tsx:164 `<Fact on={ops.engines.gemini} ...>`, :168 `<Fact on={ops.engines.claudeCli} ...>`; engine-preflight.ts:17-22 EngineAvailability = { gemini; claudeCli }.
Failover is never displayed: `grep -rln failoverFrom app/features app/_components` gives no output. Writers and readers are only app/_lib/db/interviews.ts:172, :253, :301, :374, :761-768, app/api/interview/connect/route.ts:465 and db/core.ts:842.
Untyped throws: openai.ts:315 `throw new Error(`OpenAI client_secrets ${res.status}: ...`)`, :320 (same), :326 'OpenAI did not return a client secret', :335 'no usable expiry'; elevenlabs.ts:37 env, :50 `${endpoint} responded ${res.status}`, :53 'did not return a signed_url'.
Auth posture: app/_lib/auth/public-routes.ts has no '/api/voice' (grep shows only :113 '/api/interview/connect'), and app/api/voice does not exist yet.
Existing codes reused: TOO_MANY_REQUESTS. New: VOICE_READINESS_FAILED (api-response.ts STORE_ERRORS, beside OPS_STATUS_FAILED at :128), which needs errors.VOICE_READINESS_FAILED in en, cs, de and fr.
Not a restatement: no prior challenge card, leftover-develop row or digest item covers operator-side voice readiness. The open leftover 'Fail over mid-call when the live provider drops' (L, human-routed) is client-side, in r08's VoiceInterview.tsx, and is not adopted here.
